lessons: Parse object names at the last underscore; category strings may contain underscores.
Use observed basket dimensions rather than a fixed 0.2-metre proximity test.
Assign distinct baskets to distinct categories and preserve unambiguous existing groups.
Use the arm on the source/destination side and normalize its supplied downward quaternion.
The previous post-lift RGB guard stopped every exposed run before transport; absence of visible upward motion is not reliable evidence of grasp failure.
Test center-based contact height plus the supplied tool offset, clamped to the minimum contact height, rather than adding another half object height.
Keep attempts bounded and stop on primitive errors without uncertain manipulation retries.
memory.status: Proposed corrections; task completion remains independently evaluated.

rationale: Removes the post-lift perception gate identified as the immediate stopping point in recent feedback, lowers the grasp target from the top surface to the object center plus the supplied tool offset, and avoids universally using the left arm. Basket assignment and containment use live RGB observations only. Each selected object receives one bounded transfer attempt; primitive errors end execution without retries or arbitrary releases. No grasp or sorting success is inferred from primitive completion.
